page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-48GB is a cloud server instance within UpCloud's Cloud Native family, running on KVM virtualization. The instance provides 16 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, paired with 48.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 3.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Local storage is not bundled with the instance and must be attached separately over network block storage. No dedicated graphics accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Hardware architecture features the x86_64 instruction set with support for standard extensions including AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Cache distribution includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. On synthetic stress benchmarks, single-core execution delivers 787.49 stress-ng bogo-ops, placing it in the lower performance tier, whereas multi-core throughput scales to 12555.22 bogo-ops. Memory bandwidth registers at 82.52 GB/s for large uncached reads and 39.0 GB/s for writes, supporting solid memory bus utilization.

Application and synthetic evaluation indicates strong burst text and image processing capabilities, with Geekbench single-core reaching 2089.0 and multi-core achieving 14914.0. In network application metrics, static web serving achieves 11.83 GB/s throughput, and PassMark database operations measure 9983.1 points, accompanied by 22.77 million Redis SET operations per second. Machine learning inferencing delivers 1104.1 tokens per second for prompt processing on small 135M parameter models and 56.21 tokens per second on 7B models.

Due to its shared CPU topology and lack of local storage, the instance is cost-efficient for scale-out, multi-threaded workloads that tolerate varying CPU availability rather than continuous sustained peak utilization. Best-fit use cases include parallel compilation tasks, caching layers, containerized microservices, background batch data processing, and general web serving.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-48GB is a cloud-native virtual server featuring 16 shared vCPUs based on the AMD EPYC 7542 processor at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 48.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local disk storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on attached external volumes. Benchmarks show balanced overall throughput, capturing 14914.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 28502.96 on PassMark CPU, with strong scores in text processing and image handling despite modest single-thread stress-ng scores. Memory throughput is consistent at 82.52 GB/s read, and Redis processing sustains 22.77 million SET operations per second. Configured with a 1:3 core-to-memory ratio and shared compute cores, this instance offers economical multi-threaded capacity suitable for distributed container workloads, CI/CD compilation runners, microservices, and general web applications.
